metadata.title: Secure‑Resilience IT / Server SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan governing how IT and server systems may rely on Secure‑Resilience eligibility signals without introducing unsafe recovery or unauthorized resumption.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits Secure‑Resilience Platform semantics and specializes them for IT and general-purpose server environments.

system-characteristics.system-description: IT and server systems include general-purpose compute platforms, virtual infrastructure, operating systems, middleware, and enterprise applications. This SSPP assumes that most system state is reversible, while still enforcing explicit eligibility, safety gating, and non-automatic resumption.

props.name: domain
props.remarks: Applies to non-cyber-physical, non-clinical server environments.

props.name: state-assumption
props.remarks: Most IT and server state is assumed reversible unless explicitly classified otherwise.

props.name: preferred-resilience-outcome
props.remarks: Restore or degraded operation is generally preferred over halt, subject to eligibility.

props.name: implicit-resume
props.remarks: Successful restore, backup, or failover does not imply permission to resume operation.

props.name: automation-constraint
props.remarks: Automation may restore but must not resume without explicit eligibility.

system-implementation.remarks: IT / Server resilience is implemented by applying Secure‑Resilience eligibility semantics to backup, recovery, disaster recovery, ransomware response, and continuity mechanisms. Restore and resume actions remain explicitly gated.

components.title: Backup and Recovery
components.remarks: Restore is generally permitted subject to reversibility and resume eligibility.

components.title: Disaster Recovery
components.remarks: Failover is permitted subject to resume eligibility gating.

components.title: Ransomware Resilience
components.remarks: Clean restore permitted only after containment and eligibility confirmation.

components.title: Continuity of Operations
components.remarks: Degraded modes are preferred when integrity is uncertain.

roles.title: IT / Server Resilience Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines server resilience interpretations and eligibility assumptions.

roles.title: IT / Server Resilience Governance
roles.remarks: Approves resume eligibility criteria and risk tolerance for IT systems.

roles.title: IT / Server Resilience Operations
roles.remarks: Executes recovery and continuity actions under Secure‑Resilience constraints.

roles.title: IT / Server Resilience Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors restore activity, unsafe resume attempts, and automation violations.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through Secure‑Resilience constraints applied to NIST SP 800‑53 CP controls. This SSPP introduces no additional control requirements.
